content: Cefixime, marketed under the brand name Suprax, is a cephalosporin antibiotic used to treat a wide range of bacterial infections. It is important to note that this medication is effective only against bacterial infections and will not work for viral infections such as the common cold or influenza. To use this medication, take it orally with or without food as directed by your physician, typically once daily. For children, it may be prescribed to be taken twice daily, approximately every 12 hours. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. To achieve optimal results, it is crucial to take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue taking the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days, to ensure the infection is completely eradicated. Common side effects of cefixime may include stomach upset, abdominal pain, diarrhea, nausea, gas, headache, or dizziness. These effects are usually mild and temporary. However, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the potential risks. Rarely, cefixime may cause a severe intestinal condition known as Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea, which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has ended. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may also lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to cefixime are rare but may occur. Symptoms of a severe allergic reaction include rash, itching, swelling (especially of the face, tongue, or throat), severe dizziness, or difficulty breathing. If you experience any of these symptoms, seek immediate medical attention. This is not an exhaustive list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your physician for guidance. Before taking cefixime, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to penicillins, or to other cephalosporin antibiotics (e.g., cephalexin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Cefixime may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. Additionally, the chewable form of this medication may contain aspartame, which should be considered if you have phenylketonuria (PKU). During pregnancy, cefixime should only be used when clearly needed, as its effects on an unborn child are not fully known. It is also unclear whether this medication passes into breast milk. Consult your healthcare provider for advice if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Cefixime may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as diabetic urine tests, potentially causing false results. In the event of an overdose, if someone exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store cefixime at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about cefixime. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
